MILLS ESTATE INCORPORATED
MILLS BUILDING
SAN FRANCISCO
January 28, 1927.
Joseph J. Phillips dity and county of San Francisco,
Right of Way Agent
San Francisco, California.
Dear Sir:
Mills Estate Incorporated is willing to lease to
the City and County of San Francisco, for use as a
temporary airport, one hundred and fiity (150) acres, or
thereabouts,
of its property at San Bruno heretofore
pointed out
to you.
The terms of the lease acceptable
to us are as follows:
The lease is to run for a period of three (3)
vears at a rental oi len Dollars ($10) an acre per year.
This Ten Dollars (S10) per acre per year is arrivea at as
follows:
The value of the loss of the pasturage each year
is estimated at Five Dollars ($5), and the maintenance
charges amount to Five Dollars ($5) a year.
In addition to the foregoing payments, we are to be
paid the sum of Iwenty Five Dollars ($25) per
acre at the
end of the lease in order to recondition the land for the
purposes for which it is now used. This reconditioning
involves
the plowing, discing, harrowing and reseeding of
the property.
We shall maintain the levees during the term of the
Lease Just as we have maintained them in the past, but any
lamages that may result from any breaking of the levees, or
any other cause, must be borne by yourselves.
We understand that you desire to seed some parts
if not all of the land in question, and if so such seeding
as may be done must be with our consent in order that we may
be assured that no deleterious grasses will be grown on the
property.
At the time being, we are maintaining and we shall
continue
the maintenance of a pumping plant for use in
connection with this land. Any additional expenses over and
above those now borne by us for this pumping that may be
occasioned because of your requirements, will be borne by
you•
You will be given permission to erect a water tank
on the adjacent property belonging to us, and to run a pipe
line from that property to the land in question which you
may pipe as you see fit.

Joseph J. Phillips, Esq.
January 28, 1927.
-2-
Upon the termination of the lease, you are to remove
any and all structures and improvements erected by you and
foreign substances hauled to the property, such as cinders,
gravel, etc., to make it available for our uses. In making
such removals you will be permitted to dump the waste in the
old borrow pit or sloughs on the property in question.
Trusting that the foregoing will be of assistance to
you in establishing your temporary airport, we are,
Very truly yours,
MILLS ESTATE INCORPORATED
